cases.question: 为什么最后那一项消失了？相位不是还在里面吗？
criteria: Retain the preceding RMS explanation in session history.
For a full period omega T=2 pi, so endpoint sine values agree for every phase.
Explain why this gives phase-independent RMS without claiming that phase never matters.

cases.question: Give me a small numerical example using a 10 V peak sinusoid, then explain how a 3 V DC offset changes the result.
criteria: Answer in English and preserve the follow-up context.
Without offset RMS=10/sqrt(2), about 7.071 V.
With 3 V DC offset the full-period squared mean is 9+50, so RMS=sqrt(59), about 7.681 V; distinguish this extension from the source's pure sinusoid.

Show the quadrant issue, including a vector with negative real part.
The zero phasor has no unique physical angle; do not execute the selected code.

cases.question: L05 的 RMS 相量怎么接到 L06 的复功率，以及 L08 的三相功率公式？为什么有时候有根号3，有时候没有？
criteria: For a passive single-phase load with RMS phasors S=V I*.

cases.question: The L22 baseline has 500 mm² aluminum area, 14 mm outside radius and a 75-mile route. Explain why we must not replace the metal area by πr². Calculate corrected one-conductor resistance and the two-wire loop resistance.
criteria: Use conducting area separately from the ideal magnetic surrogate radius.
Convert 75 mi to 120.7008 km and mm² to m²; corrected R is about 8.75705 ohms per conductor.
An equal two-wire loop has about 17.5141 ohms; do not carry this doubling into balanced three-phase formulas.

cases.question: For the L23 baseline distances 4, 6, 10 m and catalog GMR 10.90 mm, calculate GMD and the 75-mile phase reactance at 60 Hz. Can I average the distances arithmetically or multiply the phase reactance by two?
criteria: GMD is about 6.214465 m from the product cube root, explained by equal-length transposition of logarithmic distance terms.
Catalog GMR is used directly; L prime is about 1.269174 mH/km and route phase X about 57.7514 ohms.
No extra factor of two; balanced return is already included. Arithmetic averaging overestimates the result.

cases.question: In the L24 138 kV, 75-mile example, why does capacitance use 14 mm physical radius instead of 10.90 mm GMR? Calculate charging current and total capacitive Mvar, then explain the two π shunts and what happens at 95% voltage.
criteria: Physical radius is the lower electrostatic potential-integration bound; magnetic internal-linkage GMR is inappropriate.
Total B about 0.415293 mS gives phase charging current about 33.0882 A and three-phase capacitive supply about 7.908847 Mvar; absorbed Q is negative.
Each pi end uses B/2 with its local phase voltage. Uniform-voltage estimate is stated; 95% voltage gives 0.9025 times QC.

cases.question: For L25, explain the square four-member bundle self-distance formula, distinguishing magnetic GMR and electric radius. Is a two-member bundle two physical circuits? For the baseline 500 kV circuit on 100 MVA, give r, x and total b in pu, then explain two parallel circuits and changing only Sbase to 200 MVA.
criteria: Square self-distance includes sqrt(2) inside the fourth root, because of the diagonal; use supplied GMR for magnetics and physical radius for capacitance.
Bundle count is distinct from complete physical circuit count. Baseline r about 0.00088704 pu, x about 0.01906854 pu, total b about 1.40640538 pu.
Two identical uncoupled circuits halve series impedance and double shunt B on the same base. Doubling Sbase doubles series pu and halves shunt pu while physical circuit parameters remain fixed.
